# Source notes — Job-Order Costing (demo)
## Source
- File: none (fixture) | Sessions: 1 | Date: — | Pages: 1
## Concept inventory (lecture order)
1. Manufacturing overhead and why it is applied with a rate — p. 1
2. Predetermined overhead rate = estimated overhead ÷ estimated base — p. 1
3. Job cost sheet: DM + DL + applied overhead — p. 1
4. Cost flow entries: RM → WIP → FG → COGS — p. 1
5. Over/underapplied overhead closed to COGS — p. 1
## Formulas (verbatim, as TeX)
- POHR: `\text{POHR} = \frac{\text{estimated overhead}}{\text{estimated base}}` — p. 1
- Applied overhead: `\text{POHR} \times \text{actual base}` — p. 1
## Worked examples (exact numbers)
- POHR = 600,000 / 40,000 = 15 per DLH (→ pohr-kapitan)
- Job 101: 25,000 + 18,000 + 1,200 × 15 = 61,000 (→ job-101)
- Year end: actual 612,000 − applied 39,000 × 15 = 585,000 → underapplied 27,000 (→ close-kapitan)
## Conventions & ambiguities
- Over/underapplied overhead is closed entirely to Cost of Goods Sold (no proration).
